title: Toolbar
wrapsNative: toolbar(content:) with ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) and ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .secondaryAction or .bottomBar), with searchable(text:prompt:) for the search field and safeAreaInset(edge: .top) for a row of filters
summary: The controls above a list (search, view switch, density, export, filters) live in the system's navigation bar and bottom bar, not in a row drawn by Monarch.
whenToUse: For the tools of a list or a document screen: put the search field in searchable, the main tool in .primaryAction, less used tools in .secondaryAction (they collapse into an overflow menu), and filter chips in a safeAreaInset row under the bar.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a toolbar row inside the content; it scrolls away and repeats what the bars do. For a formatting bar inside an editor, an HStack of Toggles with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) is enough. For a call, use MonarchCallControls.
api: func toolbar<Content: ToolbarContent>(content: () -> Content) -> some View
func searchable(text: Binding<String>, placement: SearchFieldPlacement = .automatic, prompt: String) -> some View
func safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: compact width
states.description: Secondary actions collapse into the system's overflow menu; the primary action stays in the bar.

states.name: search active
states.description: The search field takes the top of the screen while it is focused (system behaviour).

states.name: disabled
states.description: A disabled item uses the system's disabled colour and is skipped by VoiceOver activation.

appearance: System bars. Items that are Buttons or Menus take the accent tint of the Monarch theme; filter chips in the inset row use the Monarch toggle button style. Correct in light, dark and both high-contrast themes because the system draws the bars.
platformNotes: The web Toolbar is a role="toolbar" row with search on the leading edge, grouped controls, trailing controls, a filters row and roving arrow-key focus. On iOS the navigation bar and the bottom bar are the toolbar: the system places, overflows and focuses the items, and a hardware keyboard moves between them with Tab. Monarch ships no toolbar type. .bottomBar and .topBarTrailing exist on iOS only; the compiled examples use the placements shared with the host build. Android uses its top app bar.
accessibility: Bar items are read as buttons with their titles; give icon-only items a title through Label or Button(_:systemImage:), which the bar shows as an icon and VoiceOver reads (system behaviour).
The search field is the system's, with its own label and clear button.
Filter chips with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) are read as toggles with their on or off value.
Bar items have the system's touch targets.
edgeCases: Too many primary items crowd the bar on a small phone; keep one or two and move the rest to .secondaryAction.
A safeAreaInset filter row with many chips scrolls horizontally; it does not wrap.
Items placed with .secondaryAction show in an overflow menu on iPhone and in the bar on iPad (system behaviour), not checked on an iPad.
The catalogue page places its items in the catalogue's own bar; the examples bring their own NavigationStack.
